newsitem.title: USA: FSI to cut workforce, take charge.
newsitem.headline: FSI to cut workforce, take charge.

text.p: FSI International Inc said Thursday it will implement certain cost-control measures, including a nine percent reduction in its workforce or about 125 positions.
It said it expects the reduction in its force to result in a pretax charge of about $300,000 in the fiscal 1997 first quarter.
The company, a manufacturer of capital equipment for the semiconductor industry, said difficult conditions in the industry prompted its actions.
FSI said it expects sales for the fiscal year ended August 31, 1996 to be more than $300 million, up 38 percent from fiscal 1995 sales of $218 million.
But it forecast its sales will decline about eight to 12 percent in fiscal 1997 compared to fiscal 1996 due to a decline in capital spending by semiconductor device manufacturers.

The company said fiscal 1996 pro forma net income is expected to be between $27.5 million and $29 million, or $1.20 to $1.25 per share, compared with $20.5 million or $1.09 per share in the prior year.
It said expected fiscal 1996 net income includes $1.5 million to $2 million in fourth-quarter pretax charges associated with eliminating or reducing the scope of certain programs.
Fiscal 1996 per share amounts reflect a greater number of shares outstanding, primarily due to stock offerings completed in February and June 1995.
FSI said its cost control measures will include mandatory furlough days, a reduction in executive compensation, a salary freeze for the entire employee base plus the workforce cuts.
In addition, the company's surface conditioning division will delay its move into a new laboratory and engineering facility in Chaska, Minn. until mid-1997 instead of moving in December 1996.

"The semiconductor industry is experiencing a slowdown, which FSI and many independent industry analysts expect to last through the middle of calendar 1997," said chairman Joel Elftmann in a statement.
"The current employment level is beyond what we can sustain during this period," Elftmann added.
Elftmann said with the semiconductor equipment industry expecting long-term growth through 2000 and beyond, FSI is "managing operations in an effort to assure profitability in fiscal 1997."

FSI said its backlog on August 31 was $113 million compared with $126 million a year earlier. "This backlog, along with recently announced orders and anticipated orders, provides us with a strong base to begin fiscal 1997," said Elftmann. "However, customers can cancel or delay orders. Backlog is not necessarily indicative of sales for future periods."
